investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC INSUFFICIENT (the homepage's own server-rendered event markup never states a year for any event), then Level 2 STRUCTURAL INSUFFICIENT: probed the site's WordPress REST API for a 'tribe/events' (The Events Calendar) route and a 'wp/v2/events' custom-post-type route; neither exists (both return 404 rest_no_route). No cleaner public JSON/API path was discoverable. No Level 3 (browser) escalation was performed (this investigation had no browser/headless tool available), and none was strictly necessary since the homepage's own markup already provides most fields honestly and completely — only the year is genuinely missing from every retained source.

probe_history.reason: A plain GET of https://frannz.eu/ (WordPress; wp-content/wp-json present) returns a large (1.28MB), fully server-rendered homepage where every upcoming show is its own custom-post-type 'events' post embedded directly in the HTML, with explicit day-of-week name, day number, month NAME (not number), and door/start times all present as real structured text (e.g. 'Donnerstag' / '15' / 'Oktober' / Einlass 19:00 / Beginn 20:00 for the sampled 'Marlene Kuntz' show) — but no year is stated anywhere in or near any event's own markup, page title, or meta description. No JSON-LD, ICS, or other machine-readable structured-data block is present anywhere on the page.

The site exposes a standard WordPress REST API root (wp-json/) but a plain GET of 'wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events' (The Events Calendar plugin's own REST route, used successfully elsewhere in this project) and 'wp-json/wp/v2/events?per_page=3' (a direct custom-post-type REST route, matching the 'type-events'/'events' CSS classes observed on each event post) both return HTTP 404 'rest_no_route' — neither route is registered/exposed. No other public JSON/API path referencing the 'events' post type or a calendar was discoverable from the retained homepage markup.

venue_reference: Frannz Club (restaurant, nightclub, bar and live-music venue inside the Kulturbrauerei complex, Schönhauser Allee 36, Prenzlauer Berg, Berlin)

identity.notes: Official identity confirmed directly from retained evidence at https://frannz.eu/: <title>Frannz Club – Restaurant, Nachtclub, Bar</title>, a standard WordPress wp-json Link header on the venue's own domain, consistent with independently-known venue facts (Kulturbrauerei, Prenzlauer Berg). Re-verified 2026-08-26 via a fresh, fully-retained homepage fetch (ev-full-homepage): the site's own footer 'Anschrift' (address) widget directly states 'FRANNZ GmbH & Co. KG / Schönhauser Allee 36 / Kulturbrauerei / 10435 Berlin' as first-party evidence of the venue's own official physical address, confirming venue_reference's address claim. Not geocoded; text only.

site_classification.platform: WordPress (wp-content, wp-json Link header present), custom theme with a bespoke 'events' custom post type rendered directly into the homepage — no known calendar plugin (The Events Calendar's own REST route is not registered) and no JSON-LD.

title.notes: Each event post's own '.event-title' element (e.g. 'Marlene Kuntz'), with a separate '.event-otitle' subtitle/category element (e.g. 'live!') also present on the same post.

start_date.notes: Each event post's own '.event-dayname' ('Donnerstag'), '.event-day' ('15') and '.event-month' ('Oktober', a full month NAME not a number) elements directly state day-of-week, day-of-month and month — but no year is stated anywhere in the retained evidence: not on the event post itself, not in the page <title>/meta, and not in a season/year heading anywhere on the page. Per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's 'Field-value basis (v1.2)' section, inferring the year from today's date or from 'the nearest plausible occurrence' would be AI_INFERENCE and can never be PROVEN — so this stays honestly PARTIAL rather than a guessed full date. A future collector-build step could still recover the year properly by following the event's own third-party ticket link (e.g. dice.fm states '15th Oct' in its own URL slug alongside a full description) — but that would make the year dependent on a third-party site rather than Frannz Club's own first-party page, which this investigation does not treat as first-party authority for this venue's own facts.

time.notes: Each event post's own '.event-start' (Beginn/start, e.g. '20:00') element is present and directly stated on every one of 108 sampled real event cards, duplicated in a desktop and a mobile-specific markup block on the same post. A '.event-entrance' (Einlass/doors, e.g. '19:00') element is also directly stated on most, but genuinely not all, cards — re-verified 2026-08-26 against the full retained homepage (ev-full-homepage): several 'Party'-type cards (e.g. 'Tannz im Frannz -auf 2 Floors', WP post id 9945) state only Beginn with no Einlass field at all. Left PROVEN because the Beginn/start time itself — the field this project's Observation contract actually models as 'start' — is directly and completely stated on every sampled card; the sometimes-absent Einlass is retained as supplementary text only, never fabricated when missing.

end.notes: No end/close time field is present anywhere in the retained event post markup.

venue_location.notes: Each event post's own sidebar states an 'Ort:' (place) value — this is literal retained text, but it reads as an internal room/area label (Frannz Club's own complex includes multiple named areas) rather than a full venue name or address. Re-verified 2026-08-26 against the full retained homepage (ev-full-homepage): the value genuinely varies per event ('Club' alone on 88 of 108 sampled cards; also observed: 'Biergarten', 'Lounge', 'Club, Lounge', 'Club, Lounge, Salon', 'Ausschank, Biergarten, Club, Lounge, Salon') — it is not the string 'Frannz Club' itself, nor an address, on any sampled card. Left PARTIAL rather than PROVEN because the retained text does not unambiguously state the full venue identity/address the way, e.g., Lido or Privatclub's own JSON-LD does. The venue's own official postal address ('Schönhauser Allee 36, Kulturbrauerei, 10435 Berlin') is separately confirmed as first-party evidence in identity.notes/ev-full-homepage, but that is the venue's own site-wide address widget, not a per-event field.

source_record_id.notes: Each event post's own <article id="post-{ID}" ...> attribute (e.g. id="post-9922" for the sampled 'Marlene Kuntz' show), also independently echoed as an HTML comment '<!-- #post-{ID} -->' immediately after each article, directly states this source's own internal WordPress post ID for that record — WordPress's own standard post_class()/the_ID() convention, not a guessed value. Re-verified 2026-08-26 (ev-post-id-stability-check): two independent, unauthenticated, plain-GET fetches of https://frannz.eu/ seconds apart returned the exact same set of 108 unique post IDs (order-independent comparison, zero differences); the only difference between the two full raw responses was an unrelated countdown-timer widget's random instance id and live-clock value, never any event's own id/title/date/time. No permalink or canonical URL exposing this ID exists on frannz.eu itself (all outbound ticket links point to third-party sellers — dice.fm, copilot.events, tickets.loft.de, and others — never to a first-party frannz.eu event page), so this ID cannot be corroborated by a second first-party representation, but its own attribute is directly stated and its stability across independent fetches is now empirically proven — satisfying the 'proven empirically' branch of the stable-identifier rule (docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md). No longer AMBIGUOUS.

event_url.notes: There is no first-party per-event permalink on frannz.eu itself — every 'Tickets' link observed points to a third-party seller's own event page (dice.fm, copilot.events, tickets.loft.de, tickets.eskapaden.net, deinetickets.de, and others vary per event), never to a frannz.eu URL.

price.notes:
Not stated for the originally-sampled 'Marlene Kuntz' event (it only names the third-party seller, 'Tickets im VVK gibt es bei dice.fm'). Re-verified 2026-08-26 against the full retained homepage (ev-full-homepage): a price IS directly stated on 16 of 108 sampled cards, in a '
{amount} {label}
' element — every observed instance is labelled 'Abendkasse' (door price), e.g. '10 €', '10.00 €', '15.00 €' (one card literally states '27,00€ €', a source-side artifact retained verbatim, not corrected) — never a VVK/advance price despite the CSS class name. Genuinely present, directly stated, and not fabricated when it appears, but absent on the large majority of cards. Left PARTIAL (present-but-inconsistent) rather than PROVEN or NOT_PRESENT.

blockers.description: No year is stated anywhere in the retained first-party evidence for any event's date — only day-of-week, day-of-month, and month name. A real collector cannot honestly resolve a full start_date from Frannz Club's own page alone; this needs an explicit human/product decision (e.g. accept an AMBIGUOUS/PARTIAL year-less date downstream, or define a documented, non-guessing policy such as 'always the next occurrence of that day+month after the page's own Last-Modified date' as a genuine DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT rule with its own retained evidence) before a collector could reach PROVEN on start_date. Still unresolved as of the 2026-08-26 re-verification. This is MAJOR, not CRITICAL: title, time, and source_record_id are all independently PROVEN, and the observation-adapter (ingestion/frannz-club/observation-adapter.mjs) honestly retains the day/month/time as TEXT_ONLY rather than fabricating a year, so downstream consumers see an honest gap rather than a wrong date.

The venue's own official postal address (Schönhauser Allee 36, Kulturbrauerei, 10435 Berlin) was confirmed as first-party evidence in the homepage's own 'Anschrift' footer widget (not geocoded). DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof evidence now retained (tests/frannz-club.test.mjs, 5 passing tests re-parsing this investigation's own retained fixtures/frannz-club-berlin/homepage.html deterministically and offline, including a regression test for a real cross-article field-mismatch bug found and fixed during adapter development) — gate 9/v1.2 satisfied. Advanced from READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF to READY_FOR_ACTIVATION.
